title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 1 (Part 1)  Teaching Experience in Virtual Garment Design Major
description:
CLO Dialogues with the Dean of the Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology! Further Understanding of the Application and Teaching of Virtual Clothing!

Video Content:
1. Virtual Humans and Digital Clothing
2. Digital Clothing in the Apparel Industry Chain
3. Teaching Applications of Virtual Clothing Design
transcript:
Good evening, everyone.  
I have been involved in digital education and research for 20 years.  
This time, I would like to share some insights and experiences, especially to explore some current trends and so on.  
Through this, I hope to communicate with all of you.  
In fact, this topic is quite broad, and I am still in the middle of this discussion.  
There are three small points I would like to mention within this large topic.  
Let’s take a look at them together.  
For example, one point concerns the currently very hot topic of women.  
The second is about the use of digital clothing within our current clothing industry chain.  
The third small point is about the education and application of digital clothing design.  
Most of these are related to digital design.  
So, let’s take a look.  

The fourth point is about virtual people.  
In recent years, virtual people, including digital people and virtual humans, have become a very hot topic.  
For example, if you search on Baidu, you can find more than 5,000 results related to this.  
There are also many results on Xiaohongshu.  
For instance, if you enter “virtual clothing” on Xiaohongshu, you can find nearly 30,000 results.  
What we often see is that there are quite a lot of results on digital people and virtual people.  
In fact, there is still a certain difference between the two.  
Digital people are those created using digital technology to produce images similar to humans.  

In 1989, the National Museum of the United States began a project called the Perspective People Project.  
These are categories of digital people.  
Perspective people represent the lowest level, which is the shape of a person.  
Subsequently, there are digital physical people and digital physiological people.  
For example, in 2001, China launched the Digital Physiological People Project.  
You can find information about it online.  
Nanfang Medical University created a digital person named Nan 1 for Chinese digital people.  
It belongs to the category of digital physiological people.  
It uses very thin chips and is produced through scanning.  
This is what the model is made of.  

In terms of clothing, we may use more virtual people.  
Virtual people refer to digital representations that have the appearance of a person, especially realistic human-like appearances.  
They can also perform behaviors and actions.  
At the same time, with the development of AI, there are also certain abilities for thoughts and cognition.  
So let’s appreciate this development together.  

What do we see in the clothing field?  
What do we usually mean when we say virtual people?  
Currently, virtual people are actually used in many industries.  
For example, on the right side here, I simply listed the financial sector, such as bank assistants, virtual buying and selling industries, and so on.  
You may have seen many of these.  

Now, let’s look at the future of virtual people.  
In fact, the first example mentioned here is one everyone will definitely talk about.  
This is Chuyin Leilai.  
She is the first virtual idol with large-scale commercial success.  
Around 2007, she appeared as a girl with a two-dimensional style image.  
She has a characteristic that fans can participate and create together.  
After collective creation by several people, Chuyin began to develop a personality, such as being cute and so on.  
Eventually, she held concerts in various places and took on some business endorsements.  
This is the first virtual person that everyone currently recognizes.  

Besides virtual idols, virtual people can also be called virtual models.  
For example, we may have seen more of them online.  
One example is A from Japan.  
She appeared on the Internet in 2018.  
In fact, she has appeared in many foreign media outlets.  
She has been involved with several major brands like Chuyin and SK-II, through her own makeup and scenes, helping these brands with publicity.  

In recent years, the domestic design and production of virtual models has been improving continuously.  
So, there are some well-known virtual models.  
One must mention here is Liu Yeji, who became popular in 2021.  
In fact, she embodies national style.  
At that time, she rose to fame on the TikTok platform.  
This kind of makeup style suddenly became popular.  
Following that, many brands cooperated with her, including Baidu and Xiaopeng Car.  
However, her current operation costs are quite high, amounting to several million yuan annually.  

Then, in 2022, during the Beijing Central Committee, there was a virtual gathering.  
She was the ambassador for the ice and snow sports promotion of He Ping Jing Jing.  
She made many young people more willing to understand the culture of ice and snow.  
During the May 4th, 2022 event, she also appeared at the May 4th evening meeting of CCTV, interacting with young people.  
She is a very positive spokesperson.  

Of course, there are many more.  
For example, there is one currently popular on the Internet with a very realistic style called Ling.  
There is also the world’s first virtual black-skinned supermodel, which you may have seen online.  
All of these look very much like real people from the outside.  
These are known as super-realistic virtual people.  

Generally, these virtual people are designed according to the character’s story, scene, and so on, and their costumes are designed accordingly.  
Of course, many others are involved to perform three-dimensional digital processing.  
So, this is also one of the current fields where digital clothing is applied.  
This is one of the small parts we mentioned earlier.  

Additionally, everyone may have noticed digital clothing products.  
This kind of clothing belongs to a field separate from virtual people’s clothing.  
At the same time, some online transactions happen in the original universe (metaverse).  
Currently, these are relatively inexpensive products.  
For example, on the far left of the picture, there is a major trading platform in China called iBox.  
There is a kind of clothing introduced there, which actually belongs to a foreign digital brand called UD.  
Its clothing line is named Change.  
When it was just released, it was relatively inexpensive.  
However, after purchase, the final price reached 99,000 yuan, which is quite expensive.  

Currently, this kind of clothing is not very popular in China due to trading restrictions, but it is still quite popular abroad.  
From this, you can see that we can perform 3D processing of this kind of clothing and assign it certain value for trading.  

The second part I want to briefly discuss is clothing CAD.  
In this part, it is inevitable to talk about clothing CAD.  
Originally, clothing CAD in the clothing industry chain was in the form of two-dimensional cutting boards, pattern pushing boards, and so forth.  
Later, it developed into three-dimensional forms.  

Here, I want to briefly talk about the development of clothing CAD technology.  
The concept of CAD was first proposed in 1959.  
It was applied in the 1970s.  
In the 1970s, the initial clothing CAD models appeared.  
At that time, cutting boards were handmade, then inputted into computers through input devices, and then plated (patterned).  

In the 1980s, PDS systems—computer cutting board systems—began to appear.  
At the end of the 1980s, the computer industry improved significantly in image and graphic processing.  
By the end of the 1990s, with the development of three-dimensional virtual technology, 3D clothing CAD began to emerge.  

In recent years, we have seen increasing possibilities to combine clothing CAD with VR technology, AI technology, and even 3D printing technology.  
So, clothing CAD has started to expand further.  

This is actually a dress made from many three-dimensional materials.  
In the clothing industry chain, we still use many products, but the main focus remains on product development and display.  

Regarding development, we all know that CAD is widely used.  
One example is the three-dimensional use of fast product prototyping.  
Here, on the left side of the picture, you can see a basic shirt.  
By changing the shape, altering the front scarf, and adjusting the sleeve length, you can quickly get two different shirts as shown on the right side.  
You can do this very quickly.  

You can identify some unsuitable or unreasonable positions and make adjustments to achieve changes in the two-dimensional sample.  
Product display includes multi-mode model display, static display, and dynamic display through dynamic embroidery.  
These two are actually useful materials.  

Then, there are some materials you may often use in teaching about the construction of excellent cultural traditions, especially using digital innovation to promote excellent traditional design.  

There are also some materials not suitable for this kind of design.  
So, you can use digital design to recreate traditional designs.  
There are materials you can use to make this kind of design.  
This is one of its advantages.  

Here, there are some projects we completed.  
On the left, there are new discoveries of three new piles (ancient burial mounds) from the past three thousand years.  
What was the specific clothing of that era?  
In fact, no one knows precisely at this moment.  
But we created these three new clothing designs based on research and innovation.  

In the past, many people were interested in this kind of clothing.  
This kind of clothing was very popular among people interested in traditional clothing history.  
This clothing was also presented using 3D technology.  
Eventually, this kind of clothing won a gold and first prize award.  

In fact, the effect of 3D and 2D design is completely different, with 3D being more realistic than actual clothing.  
The real clothing looks better, but the 3D presentation is very close.  

This kind of clothing was very popular among those interested in traditional clothing.  
It was also popular among people who wanted to start designing this kind of clothing.  

[Note: The original text contained numerous repeated sentences about popularity and interest in the clothing, which have been consolidated here to maintain clarity and coherence.]

chunks.content: ## Overview of Digital Education and Virtual Garment Design This section introduces key themes in digital garment design education, focusing on trends such as virtual people, digital clothing in the apparel industry, and education related to digital design. It sets the stage for understanding how digital technologies are influencing garment design and virtual modeling. The speaker has over 20 years of experience in digital education and research. The discussion covers four main points: 1. The role and emergence of women in digital garment design. 2. The integration of digital clothing within the apparel industry chain. 3. Education and practical application of digital clothing design. 4. The rise and significance of virtual people (virtual humans and digital people) in various industries. These topics are interrelated around the broader theme of digital design technologies. --- ## Virtual People and Digital Humans in the Clothing Industry This section explains the concepts of digital people and virtual humans, their distinctions, historical projects, and their applications in fashion and other industries. - **Digital People vs. Virtual People**: - *Digital people* are digitally created human-like images focusing primarily on human shape and physiological features. - *Virtual people* include more advanced features such as realistic appearances, behaviors, and AI-driven cognition. - **Historical Context**: - The U.S. National Museum launched the *Perspective People Project* in 1989, categorizing digital people by complexity (shape, physical, physiological). - China’s *Digital Physiological People Project* (2001) produced "Nan 1," a digital physiological human created using thin chips and scanning tech by Nanfang Medical University. - **Applications in Clothing**: Virtual people are widely used across industries, including finance (e.g., virtual bank assistants) and commerce (virtual buying/selling). In clothing, they serve as avatars, models, and promotional figures. - **Examples of Virtual People**: - *Chuyin Leilai*: The first large-scale commercial virtual idol emerging around 2007 with a two-dimensional style. Developed personality traits through fan collaboration and engaged in concerts and endorsements. - *Virtual Models*: - *A* from Japan (2018) gained media attention and brand collaborations (e.g., SK-II). - *Liu Yeji*, a Chinese virtual model popularized in 2021 on TikTok, known for embodying national style and high-profile endorsements (Baidu, Xiaopeng Car). Annual operation costs for Liu Yeji are several million yuan. - Other notable virtual people include *Ling* (realistic style) and the world’s first virtual black-skinned supermodel. - **Technical Aspects**: Virtual people are often designed with detailed character backstories and scene-based costumes, utilizing 3D digital processing to enhance realism. --- ## Digital Clothing Products and the Metaverse Marketplace This section discusses digital clothing as distinct from clothing worn by virtual people, focusing on product design, trading platforms, and market trends. - Digital clothing products are sold and traded in virtual environments such as the metaverse. - Example platform: *iBox* in China hosts digital clothing lines like *Change* by the foreign brand *UD*. - Prices can vary significantly; the *Change* collection, initially inexpensive, saw resale prices reach up to 99,000 yuan. - Despite limited popularity in China due to trading restrictions, digital clothing enjoys greater demand internationally.

chunks.content: --- ## Digital Clothing Products and the Metaverse Marketplace This section discusses digital clothing as distinct from clothing worn by virtual people, focusing on product design, trading platforms, and market trends. - Digital clothing products are sold and traded in virtual environments such as the metaverse. - Example platform: *iBox* in China hosts digital clothing lines like *Change* by the foreign brand *UD*. - Prices can vary significantly; the *Change* collection, initially inexpensive, saw resale prices reach up to 99,000 yuan. - Despite limited popularity in China due to trading restrictions, digital clothing enjoys greater demand internationally. - These garments undergo 3D processing and are assigned value for trading, showing the convergence of fashion and digital asset markets. --- ## Evolution and Application of Clothing CAD Technology This section covers the development and current state of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) in the garment industry, highlighting its transformation from 2D to 3D and integration with emerging technologies. - **Historical Development**: - CAD was first proposed in 1959 and applied in the 1970s. - Early clothing CAD involved 2D cutting boards and hand-input patterning. - The 1980s saw the emergence of PDS (computer cutting board systems). - By the 1990s, advancements in virtual technology enabled the rise of 3D clothing CAD. - **Recent Trends**: - Integration with Virtual Reality (VR), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and 3D printing expands CAD capabilities. - CAD supports rapid prototyping and product development, enabling quick adjustments to garment shape, style, and details (e.g., sleeve length, scarf design). - **Product Development and Display**: - CAD is used to detect design flaws and make corrections before physical production. - Product display includes static and dynamic modes, with dynamic embroidery showcasing movement and texture. --- ## Digital Innovation in Traditional Clothing Design This section explores the use of digital design to preserve and innovate on traditional cultural garments, emphasizing the role of 3D technology in historical research and fashion education. - Digital design can recreate and innovate traditional clothing using appropriate digital materials. - Some materials and design elements are more suitable for digital reproduction, while others are less compatible. - **Case Study – Archaeological Clothing Reconstruction**: - Researchers recreated clothing based on three newly discovered ancient burial mounds dating back 3,000 years. - Although precise historical clothing details are unknown, the digital designs are informed by research and creative innovation. - These 3D reconstructions won a gold and first prize award for their realistic presentation. - **3D vs. 2D Design**: - 3D designs offer a more realistic representation compared to traditional 2D patterns. - While real garments may look better, 3D digital clothing closely approximates real-life appearance and is valuable for education and design initiation. - Traditional clothing digitally recreated through these methods has garnered significant interest among enthusiasts and designers, supporting cultural heritage through modern technology. --- # Summary This document covers key aspects of virtual garment design education and practice, including the rise of virtual people, digital clothing markets, CAD technology evolution, and digital innovation in traditional costume design.
